# Chris Lam

> Product engineer and designer, 14 years. Designs, builds, and ships end to end with no handoff. Building voice AI at y30. Open to senior IC roles, full-time, on small, fast, AI-native teams in AI, voice, and product engineering.

Chris Lam (Christopher Lam) is a product engineer and designer based in Honolulu, remote-first, with Bay Area and Seattle availability when needed. He has spent 14 years as the first, sole, or early designer-engineer in the room across healthcare, marketplaces, and consumer software. He is AI-native: he steers product, architecture, and systems while using AI agents to implement, owning the judgment, code review, and safety gates. He is currently Co-Founder and CPTO at y30 (voice AI for older adults and their caregivers) and is open to senior IC roles, full-time, looking for a long-term home with depth and continuity over range.

His exits, framed honestly and never as a trophy count: he was early at Clover Health and GoodRx (both later IPO'd), a rescue hire at Sharecare during its acquisition (which then went public), and did the 2014 TaskRabbit rebrand before IKEA acquired it. The signal is repeated high ownership at early or critical stages, not an exit count.

## Selected outcomes
- Clover Health (2nd designer, later IPO'd): ~7-8x lift in nurse visit-related revenue, ~2 hours saved per nurse per day.
- GoodRx / Iodine (first full-time designer, later IPO'd): coupon conversion 2% to 5%; GoodRx Research dataviz referenced in the New York Times and on Good Morning America and ABC News; Webby 2018.
- TaskRabbit (later acquired by IKEA): owned the Tasker experience; NPS recovered from about -5 to the mid-50s.
- Amazon: prototyped the buy-and-gift Prime flow that contributed to 1M+ new subscribers.
- Modus Create: shipped dark mode for JIRA and Confluence Cloud, 500K+ enterprise users.
- y30: built the voice pipeline (multi-provider, deep fallback) and a model-independent safety floor; 1,389 commits, 127 test files.
- PlaySesh: built 0 to 1 solo; 5,120 users across 121 Discord servers, 1,302 MAU, all organic.

## Selected engineering (systems depth, not commit counts)
- PlaySesh: authored the core real-time engine, a custom operation-based sync protocol on Cloudflare Durable Objects (authoritative ordering, hand-written WebSocket reconnection), after moving the product off an off-the-shelf canvas library. Primary engineer on the codebase.
- Evolve, Die, Repeat (solo Lua/Love2D game): a solver that proves every procedurally generated level is completable via a reachability search over the player's jump physics; from-scratch headless test harness, about 1,568 tests.
- y30: conversation flow as a deterministic state machine with the language model scoped to phrasing and warmth, plus a model-independent rule-based safety floor; about half of routing resolves with no model call.
- Engineering judgment: built y30's first version in TypeScript, then deliberately rewrote it in Python to fit the real-time voice framework, carrying the architecture and safety model across as a spec.
- Hand-built without AI: this site and its voice agent are vanilla JavaScript, no framework, down to audio codec detection and mobile keyboard handling.
- y30: an automated eval flywheel grades every conversation against a rubric and auto-files regressions as issues (metadata only, no transcript or PHI), so quality drops are caught without a human in the loop.
- y30: real-time emotion-aware delivery, the agent reads emotional cues and adapts its voice in the moment (for example, softening when a conversation turns to grief).
- y30: a provider-resilient voice pipeline that degrades gracefully across multiple STT, LLM, and TTS providers plus a separate speech-to-speech fallback, so a live call never breaks when one dependency fails.
